title: Counting a large text
description:
Write `top_words(text, k)` that returns the `k` most common words in a large text as a list of `{ word, count }` pairs, most common first and ties in alphabetical order. Words are runs of letters (`%a+`), compared in lower case.

Also write `stats(text)` returning `words` (the total), `distinct` and `longest` (the first longest word, lower-case).

The text in the tests has 300,000 words: count with one table lookup per word (no searching through lists), use locals for library functions in the loop, and sort only the distinct words.

starter.solution.lua:
function top_words(text, k)
    local seen = {}
    for w in text:gmatch("%a+") do
        local found = false
        for _, item in ipairs(seen) do
            if item[1] == w:lower() then item[2] = item[2] + 1; found = true end
        end
        if not found then seen[#seen + 1] = { w:lower(), 1 } end
    end
    return seen
end

function stats(text)
    return { words = 0, distinct = 0, longest = "" }
end

solution.solution.lua:
local function count(text)
    local counts, total, longest = {}, 0, ""
    local lower = string.lower
    for w in text:gmatch("%a+") do
        w = lower(w)
        counts[w] = (counts[w] or 0) + 1
        total = total + 1
        if #w > #longest then longest = w end
    end
    return counts, total, longest
end

function top_words(text, k)
    local counts = count(text)
    local list = {}
    for w, n in pairs(counts) do list[#list + 1] = { w, n } end
    table.sort(list, function(a, b)
        if a[2] ~= b[2] then return a[2] > b[2] end
        return a[1] < b[1]
    end)
    local out = {}
    for i = 1, math.min(k, #list) do out[i] = list[i] end
    return out
end

function stats(text)
    local counts, total, longest = count(text)
    local distinct = 0
    for _ in pairs(counts) do distinct = distinct + 1 end
    return { words = total, distinct = distinct, longest = longest }
end

hints: `counts[w] = (counts[w] or 0) + 1` counts a word with one lookup; only after the loop turn the table into a list to sort (lesson 8.05).
`local lower = string.lower` before the loop saves looking up `string` and `lower` 300,000 times.
unitTests:
test("small text", function()
    local t = "The cat sat. The cat sat on the mat, THE end."
    check_eq(top_words(t, 3), { { "the", 4 }, { "cat", 2 }, { "sat", 2 } })
    check_eq(stats(t), { words = 11, distinct = 6, longest = "the" })
    check_eq(top_words("", 3), {})
end)

test("a large text quickly", function()
    local words = { "lua", "table", "string", "metatable", "coroutine", "closure" }
    local parts = {}
    for i = 1, 300000 do parts[i] = words[(i * i) % 6 + 1] end
    local text = table.concat(parts, " ")
    local start = os.clock()
    local top = top_words(text, 2)
    local s = stats(text)
    check(os.clock() - start < 2, "took too long")
    check_eq(s.words, 300000)
    check_eq(s.distinct, 4)
    check_eq(s.longest, "coroutine")
    check_eq(#top, 2)
    check(top[1][2] >= top[2][2])
end)
